clauses.text: Two statuses: a DECIDED record carries a decision from its kind's set and a null error; an ERROR record a null decision and an error from the five reserved codes (before selection: ERR_MALFORMED_INPUT, ERR_RULE_NOT_SELECTED; during evaluation: ERR_EVALUATOR_UNAVAILABLE, ERR_TIMEOUT, ERR_INTERNAL). Both or neither is ENVELOPE_MIXED.

Fail closed: effectiveDecision is the decision on DECIDED and the kind's fail-closed value on ERROR, stored and recomputed, otherwise EFFECTIVE_MISMATCH; never ALLOW, PASS or APPROVED on an ERROR record.
Absence is not allow: a decision point that gets no record within its deadline writes an ERROR record with ERR_TIMEOUT and acts on the fail-closed value; an outage never surfaces as ALLOW.
Error reasons stay apart: an ERR_ reason code on a DECIDED record, or a policy reason code on an ERROR record, is ERROR_AS_DECISION.
Version pins: a DECIDED record names its rule and version; an ERROR record may carry a null rule only with the two codes raised before selection; otherwise RULE_VERSION_MISSING.

A model never lowers and never approves: on APPROVAL the verified decision maker decides alone and a model-only APPROVED or a model-only lift is MODEL_APPROVAL (E6a); on the other kinds the decision is the most restrictive deterministic contribution and a lower one is MODEL_LOWERED (E6b); two TRANSFORM contributions with TRANSFORM as the decision are TRANSFORM_CONFLICT (E6c).
Closed values: a kind or decision outside the closed sets is read as the kind's fail-closed value; no default branch maps to ALLOW, PASS or APPROVED.
transform is non-null exactly when effectiveDecision is TRANSFORM, otherwise TRANSFORM_MISMATCH.
The APPROVAL record's decision is APPROVED, made by the verified decision maker (E6a).
It is unexpired at the time of the effect, under HR-APPROVAL's expiry rules (its O3).
Its subject's scopeDigest, subjectDigest and revision equal the ESCALATE record's.
Its escalationRef equals digest(the ESCALATE record): an approval of one escalation cannot lift a later one on the same action.

The ESCALATE record has not been lifted before: an ESCALATE record is lifted at most once, and a second approval naming a lifted escalation is LIFT_REFUSED. A lift is recorded by the effect it permits, in the same commit as the effect (H14's same-commit order); a crash before that commit leaves it unlifted (E1, folded).

ruleFamilies.name: The lift rule (a consumer rule over two records)

settlements.text: The schema name rides on each record as schemaVersion (MAS-RA-001's form).
R00's registry: one policy reason code per kind and decision value (KIND_DECISION); the ERR_ prefix is reserved for the five error codes (E4).
R00 fixes the check order of the eight single-record codes and one vector per code (r2 section 6's last line); LIFT_REFUSED is the consumer rule's result over two records.
P8's two chained records are two RECORD cases, P8a and P8b; the checker binds P8b's supersedes and valueBeforeDigest to P8a's.
APPROVAL's verified decision maker is HR-APPROVAL's decidedBy, a HUMAN reviewer with an id digest.

The TLA+ models' crash, race and repeat actions are the seven test cases in tests/test_decision_record.py, through the model's Consumer seam; Revoke is listed with no case (HR-APPROVAL's later effect-time recheck packet owns it).

outOfScope: ACCESS_REVIEW (a v2 kind with an attestation outcome, r2 section 3).
That a decision point runs the rule its record names (H16, H13).
That a point without a deadline writes ERR_TIMEOUT.
Any H14 ledger write; the record is bound to it by the same-commit order only.
